h1: Blue Lapan Inn Pattani — a minimalist hostel inside the PSU campus, dorm beds from ฿350
intro: If you're in town for something at Prince of Songkla University's Pattani campus and want a clean, cheap bed as close to the gate as possible, Blue Lapan Inn Pattani is a name that keeps coming up in the Sai Maw neighbourhood. It's a small minimalist-style guest house on Charoenpradit Road (the road locals call Sai Maw), right inside the PSU Pattani campus. You'll find both gender-separated dorm beds and private rooms here. Rooms are clean, with a fridge, electric kettle, TV, a reading corner and free Wi-Fi, and you can walk to Green Market, Lotus's and local cafes. Dorm beds start at around ฿350 per person, private rooms from around ฿690 per night.

body.html: Blue Lapan Inn Pattani is a small guest house taking daily bookings at 181 Charoenpradit Road — the street locals call Sai Maw — in Rusamilae, Mueang Pattani, inside the Prince of Songkla University (PSU) Pattani campus. It originally opened to host parents visiting their student children, academics and speakers coming for conferences, and the general public with business at the university. The thing guests agree on is the location: it puts you within walking distance of the faculties, lecture buildings, Green Market and the cluster of cafes that keep popping up along Sai Maw.

The clever part is that you get both dorm beds and private rooms in one place. The dorm side is bunk beds in gender-separated zones, priced per bed — lower bunks from around ฿350, upper bunks from around ฿400 — which suits solo travellers on a budget. Private rooms range from single and double beds up to a King. Rooms are decorated in a clean, bright minimalist style with comfy beds, a fridge, electric kettle, iron, TV and a reading corner — a small touch guests appreciate. Every room has air-conditioning and free Wi-Fi.
"Clean room, cute decor, easy on the wallet, and it's right inside the university — you can walk to Green Market and the coffee shops. Super convenient for visiting my kid at PSU."

On location, if your main business is around PSU Pattani, this is about as well-placed as it gets among stays in the area — you're inside the campus, so no driving in and out several times a day. Around you it's a walk to Green Market (the campus night market), Lotus's, 7-Eleven and the pretty cafes that keep opening along Sai Maw. At night the area is quiet and pleasant, with the string lights the owners like to post about. For people visiting students, sitting exams, attending seminars, or backpackers wanting a cheap bed near the university, a location like this is hard to find.

To be straight with you, this is a small hostel-style guest house, not a full hotel, so there are limits worth knowing before you book. There's no breakfast, no swimming pool and no 24-hour front desk. Check-in is limited to roughly 14:00–21:00 — if you arrive later you'll need to contact the property in advance about collecting a key. There aren't many rooms, so during graduation or exam periods they fill up fast and you should book ahead. And because it sits inside the campus, driving in and out may mean passing the guard post and following PSU's rules — confirm parking and access with the property first.

One more thing to set expectations on: Blue Lapan Inn is a small place that takes bookings mainly through social channels — Facebook, LINE and phone — rather than the big international booking sites. That means online reviews are still thinner than the larger city hotels. The overall sentiment from people who've stayed leans positive on cleanliness, the cute decor and value for money. But given its size and simple service, if you're expecting hotel-level service or a big pile of reviews to compare, set your expectations to a hundreds-of-baht hostel-style stay.

Overall, Blue Lapan Inn Pattani suits budget travellers who value being close to PSU Pattani, cleanliness and a light price over luxury facilities. If you're here for university business, visiting family who study here, or a solo traveller after a cheap dorm bed within walking distance of everything, this is a tidy fit. But if your trip is about exploring the old town or you want hotel-style service, look instead at stays in central Pattani.

faq.q: Where is Blue Lapan Inn Pattani and what's nearby?
faq.a: Blue Lapan Inn Pattani is at 181 Charoenpradit Road (Sai Maw road), Rusamilae, Mueang Pattani, inside the Prince of Songkla University (PSU) Pattani campus. You can walk to the faculties, Green Market, Lotus's and 7-Eleven. Rusamilae Beach is about 7 minutes' drive, and the old town and Lim Ko Niao Shrine about 10–12 minutes' drive. It's ideal for people with business around the university.

faq.q: How much does Blue Lapan Inn Pattani cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Dorm beds start at around ฿350/person (lower bunk) and ฿400 (upper bunk), in gender-separated zones. Private rooms start at around ฿690/night for a single, with a double around ฿750 and a King around ฿850. Prices vary by season — contact the property before booking.

faq.q: How do I book Blue Lapan Inn Pattani, and is there breakfast?
faq.a: It takes bookings mainly via Facebook (Bluelapan), LINE and phone rather than the big booking sites, so contact ahead about availability and key collection. There's no breakfast included, but you can walk to Green Market, Lotus's, 7-Eleven and the Sai Maw cafes. Every room has a fridge, kettle and free Wi-Fi.

faq.q: Who is Blue Lapan Inn Pattani best for?
faq.a: It's best for budget travellers, parents visiting students, people here for exams/seminars, and solo travellers who want a cheap bed within walking distance of PSU Pattani. If you need breakfast, a pool or full hotel-style service, look at a hotel in central Pattani instead.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Blue Lapan Inn Pattani like?
faq.a: Rooms are decorated in a bright, clean minimalist style with comfy beds, a fridge, electric kettle, iron, TV and a reading corner. There are both gender-separated bunk dorms and private rooms in several sizes. Note it's a small place: check-in is limited to roughly 14:00–21:00 and there's no 24-hour front desk.
